topic: Type Aliases with typedef and using in Modern C++
explanation: In C++, type aliases are used to create alternative names for existing types, improving code readability and portability. Modern C++ (C++11 and beyond) introduces 'using' as a more versatile and clearer way to define type aliases compared to the traditional 'typedef'. Type aliases are especially useful in template programming and when working with complex or implementation-defined types, allowing developers to abstract away implementation details and write more maintainable code.
keywords: C++ type alias, typedef vs using, using alias, alias template
